chunks: And the Shaykh informed me, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Miskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the kurr of water: how much is its measure? He said: “When the water is three spans and a half by the like of it, three spans and a half, and in its depth in the ground, then that is the kurr of water.”

As for the report narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, all together from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: “If the water is more than a rāwiyah, nothing renders it impure, whether something decomposed in it or did not decompose in it, unless an odor comes to it that overcomes the odor of the water.”

So there is no contradiction in it with what we narrated and mentioned first, because he said: if the water is more than a rāwiyah. Thus he clarified that it only does not bear impurity when it exceeds a rāwiyah, and it is not impossible that by this increase he meant that by which the completion of the kurr is attained.

And as for the report narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “The kurr of water is approximately like this jar of mine,” and he pointed to a jar among those jars that used to be in al-Madīnah.
So it is not impossible that the jar held an amount of water equal to a kurr, and this is not far-fetched.

key_terms.أَشْبَارٍ: spans, a unit of measure used to define the dimensions of kurr
key_terms.الْكُرِّ: the legal measure of a large quantity of water in ritual purity law
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the substance whose purity ruling is being discussed
key_terms.حُبٍّ: a large jar used as a practical comparison for the amount of kurr
key_terms.رَاوِيَةٍ: a water-container quantity used as a comparative measure in another report
key_terms.عُمْقِهِ: its depth, part of the dimensional description of the water quantity
key_terms.نَجَاسَةً: ritual impurity affecting legal purity rulings
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: renders it impure, referring to the effect of najasah on water

ai.seo_question: What is the measure of kurr water in Shia hadith, and how are other narrations about large amounts of water reconciled with it?
ai.summary: This text discusses the legal measure of kurr water and gives its dimensions as a standard for determining when water is not rendered impure by contact with najasah unless its smell changes. It also reconciles other reports mentioning a rāwiyah or a large jar by explaining that they can be understood consistently with the kurr measure.
